Qinzhou Ruifeng Vanadium-Titanium-Iron Technology Co., Ltd. v. Beihang University — dispute over technology contract

Ruling Summary

1. In determining whether a party entrusted with a technology development contract has committed fraudulent acts, it is necessary to respect the characteristics and patterns of technology development activities themselves, to distinguish between different stages of technology development, and to use the facts known at the time of contract execution and the circumstances that the entrusted party could reasonably have foreseen at that time as the criteria for judging whether it fabricated or concealed true information.

2. The understanding of a product, especially an intermediate product, must take into account both the research and development stage in which it is situated and the specific process to which it corresponds.

3. Technology development costs include, but are not limited to, expenses related to test equipment. Moreover, technology development costs are merely one factor in determining the price of a technology development contract. The advanced nature of the technological achievement, the extent of its implementation, transformation, and application, the rights and interests enjoyed and responsibilities borne by the parties, and the economic benefits of the technological achievement are also important considerations for pricing a technology development contract, just as technology development costs are.

4. The judgment on whether to invest in a large-scale industrial pilot project, although inseparable from an understanding of the technology and the project, is essentially a commercial judgment. Commercial analyses such as the estimation of project output value, the calculation of project costs, and the prediction of project profits shall be completed by the investor.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2015) Min San Zhong Zi No. 8

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Qinzhou Ruifeng Vanadium-Titanium-Iron Technology Co., Ltd. Place of domicile: Qinnan Area, Qinzhou Imported Resources Processing Zone, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Chen Keying, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Cheng Shaofei, lawyer at Beijing Haoheng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Dai Qidong, lawyer at Liaoning Baoyu Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Beihang University. Place of domicile: No. 37 Xueyuan Road, Haidian District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Xu Huibin, President of the University.

Agent ad litem: Lu Huimin, Professor of the University.

Agent ad litem: Min Jihong, lawyer at Beijing Yingke Law Firm.

Appellant Qinzhou Ruifeng Vanadium-Titanium-Iron Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qinzhou Ruifeng Company), in a dispute over a technology contract with Respondent Beihang University (hereinafter referred to as Beihang University), appealed against the Civil Judgment (hereinafter referred to as the First Instance Judgment) (2014) Gao Min Zhi Chu Zi No. 3421 rendered by the Beijing High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the First Instance Court) to this Court. After this Court filed the case on November 23, 2015, it formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a hearing. The Appellant Qinzhou Ruifeng Company and the Respondent Beihang University appeared before the court. This case has now been concluded.

Appeal requests of Qinzhou Ruifeng Company: 1. Set aside the First Instance Judgment; 2. Amend the judgment in accordance with the law to support the claims of Qinzhou Ruifeng Company, i.e., set aside the "Technology Development (Entrustment) Contract" numbered Qin Rui Jian-001, the "Technical Appendix," and the subsequently signed "Contract Appendix (1)", "Contract Appendix (2)", and "Supplementary Technical Appendix" between Qinzhou Ruifeng Company and Beihang University; order Beihang University to immediately return the technology development funding of RMB 57,960,000 already paid by Qinzhou Ruifeng Company and compensate Qinzhou Ruifeng Company for economic losses of RMB 227,040,000; 3. Order Beihang University to bear all litigation costs of this case. Facts and Reasons: (1) The First Instance Court admitted the "Science and Technology Achievement Appraisal Certificate" (hereinafter referred to as the "Appraisal Certificate") issued by the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association, with number Zhong Se Xie Ke Jian Zi [2008] No. 113, and based on this, found that the technology described in the contract had no fatal defects. This lacks support. 1. The appraisal lacked basic documents. According to the "List of Main Technical Documents and Their Sources" section in the Appraisal Certificate, six documents, including the "Appraisal Outline for the Comprehensive Utilization Technology of Vanadium-Titanium Magnetite Sand", the "Technical Report on the Comprehensive Utilization Technology of Vanadium-Titanium Magnetite Sand", the "Economic Benefit Analysis Report on the Comprehensive Utilization Technology of Vanadium-Titanium Magnetite Sand", the "Technology Development Contract", the "Test Report", and the "Science and Technology Novelty Search Report", were the basic documents for this appraisal. However, none of these six documents were found in the entire archives of this appraisal obtained by Qinzhou Ruifeng Company from the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association. 2. The appraisal procedure was illegal. The "Expert Test Report of the Appraisal Committee" section in the Appraisal Certificate states "None", indicating that the Appraisal Committee did not test the key links of the comprehensive utilization technology of vanadium-titanium magnetite sand in accordance with the relevant provisions of the "Science and Technology Achievement Appraisal Measures" of the former State Science and Technology Commission of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Science and Technology Achievement Appraisal Measures"). 3. The determination in the Appraisal Certificate regarding the product obtained from deep reduction smelting in the electric furnace contradicts the data recorded in the "Application Report for the Industrialization Demonstration Project of Vanadium-Titanium-Iron Separation Technology" (hereinafter referred to as the "Demonstration Project Application Report") compiled by Beihang University and Beihang University's own statements. According to the industry standard YS/T298-2007 for high titanium slag approved by the National Development and Reform Commission, the titanium dioxide content of high titanium slag must be higher than 80%. The Appraisal Certificate determined that the product after deep reduction smelting in the electric furnace was high titanium slag with a titanium dioxide content of 87.29%. Pages 32 and 70 of the Demonstration Project Application Report state that the industrial demonstration project for vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology planned to use ore sand with a titanium dioxide content of 10.64%, with an annual processing capacity of 600,000 tons of ore sand and a titanium slag output of 137,500 tons. Based on the law of conservation of mass, the titanium dioxide content of the titanium slag obtained from the project could only be less than 46.4%. Beihang University also clearly acknowledged in the "Feasibility Study Report (Supplementary Report) for the Industrial Demonstration Project of Vanadium-Titanium-Iron Separation Technology" (hereinafter referred to as the "Demonstration Project Supplementary Report") and during the first instance trial of this case that the product obtained from electric furnace smelting was only titanium slag. Similarly, based on the data on vanadium pentoxide content in the raw material chemical composition table on page 32 of the Demonstration Project Application Report, applying the law of conservation of mass, it can be inferred that the product obtained from the project was only vanadium-containing pig iron, not high-vanadium molten iron as stated in the Appraisal Certificate. 4. The "Review Opinion on the Feasibility Study Report for the Industrial Demonstration Project of Vanadium-Titanium-Iron Separation Technology of Qinzhou Ruifeng Vanadium-Titanium-Iron Technology Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as the "Nonferrous Metals Association Review Opinion") issued by the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association for the Demonstration Project Supplementary Report can also indirectly prove that the Appraisal Certificate should not be admitted. As mentioned above, the Demonstration Project Supplementary Report constitutes a negation of the Appraisal Certificate, and the Nonferrous Metals Association Review Opinion affirms the Demonstration Project Supplementary Report. Therefore, the Nonferrous Metals Association Review Opinion also constitutes a negation of the Appraisal Certificate. Given that some experts who issued the Appraisal Certificate and the Nonferrous Metals Association Review Opinion are the same, it should be determined that the Appraisal Certificate has been overturned and therefore should not be admitted. (2) The First Instance Court did not admit the "Expert Review Opinion on the Feasibility Study Report for the Industrial Demonstration Project of Vanadium-Titanium Separation Technology of Qinzhou Ruifeng Vanadium-Titanium-Iron Technology Co., Ltd. in Guangxi" (hereinafter referred to as the "Guangxi Transportation Company Expert Review Opinion") formed after the technical exchange meeting on the Qinzhou Ruifeng vanadium-titanium magnetite project organized by Guangxi Transportation Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guangxi Transportation Company). This lacks support. The Appraisal Certificate was an appraisal opinion for the technology of producing high-vanadium molten iron and high titanium slag using vanadium-titanium magnetite sand as raw material, while the Guangxi Transportation Company Expert Review Opinion was a technical review opinion for producing synthetic rutile using smelted titanium slag as raw material, and it is unrelated to the Appraisal Certificate. The experts who participated in forming the Guangxi Transportation Company Expert Review Opinion did not see the Appraisal Certificate and were not aware that Beihang University had fabricated vanadium-containing molten iron and smelted titanium slag as high-vanadium molten iron and high titanium slag, submitted this as a scientific and technological achievement for appraisal, and obtained the Appraisal Certificate. The First Instance Court arbitrarily fabricated a connection between the two and, on the grounds that the Appraisal Certificate was more authoritative, held that the Guangxi Transportation Company Expert Review Opinion alone was insufficient to prove that the technology provided by Beihang University had fatal defects. This lacks support. (3) Beihang University fabricated a total project output value exceeding RMB 1.6 billion, leading to Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's misjudgment of investment, and thus constituted fraud against Qinzhou Ruifeng Company. 1. Beihang University fabricated the output value of titanium slag. Before the contract was signed, Beihang University stated on page 70 of the Demonstration Project Application Report that the market price of titanium slag was RMB 5,262/ton. However, after the contract was signed, it explicitly stated in the Demonstration Project Supplementary Report that "currently, smelted titanium slag has not yet been accepted by the market as a product," which admitted that titanium slag had no market value. 2. Beihang University fabricated the output value of vanadium-containing pig iron. Beihang University stated on page 70 of the Demonstration Project Application Report that one of the project products was ferrovanadium, with a market value of RMB 5,076/ton. However, as mentioned above, the project could only produce vanadium-containing pig iron. The market value of vanadium-containing pig iron is only RMB 2,000/ton. (4) Beihang University falsely reported technology development costs and fraudulently obtained huge sums of technology research and development funding. In the Demonstration Project Application Report, Beihang University reported that the manufacturing cost of the entire industrial production line was RMB 315 million. Qinzhou Ruifeng Company and Beihang University entered into the contract in question based on this. However, the total cost for Beihang University to subcontract the production line manufacturing project to China Steel Research New Metallurgy High-Tech Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as New Metallurgy Company) was only RMB 170.2 million. The falsely reported technology development costs amounted to as much as RMB 144.8 million. (5) The First Instance Court's failure to support Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's application for a re-appraisal of the comprehensive utilization technology of vanadium-titanium magnetite sand lacks support. Whether the content of the Appraisal Certificate is true and whether the technology described therein is achievable is key to determining whether Beihang University constituted fraud. As mentioned above, the Appraisal Certificate is not achievable in practice and violates the laws of natural science. Beihang University also denied its own technical products in the Demonstration Project Supplementary Report and its first instance statement in this case. Under these circumstances, the First Instance Court should have granted Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's application for a re-appraisal of the technology in question. In summary, the real products of Beihang University's so-called comprehensive utilization technology of vanadium-titanium magnetite sand are low-market-value vanadium-containing molten iron and smelted titanium slag with no market value. These are far from the product quality recorded in the Appraisal Certificate, the product market value recorded in the Demonstration Project Application Report, and the product quality indicators recorded in the contract in question. Beihang University fabricated the technical products and technical economic benefits, obtained the Appraisal Certificate through false technical content, and then used the authority of the Appraisal Certificate to cover up the truth of the falsification at the source of the technology, inducing Qinzhou Ruifeng Company to invest in the industrial demonstration project of this technology, in order to achieve the purpose of defrauding huge sums of technology development funding. Its conduct constituted fraud.

Beihang University argued: (1) The First Instance Court's admission of the Appraisal Certificate was proper. 1. The basic documents for this appraisal were complete. During the first instance trial of this case, Beihang University clearly stated that Beihang University retained all six technical documents listed in the "List of Main Technical Documents and Their Sources" section of the Appraisal Certificate. Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's claim that the appraisal lacked basic documents is unfounded, as it did not apply to the First Instance Court within the statutory period to obtain the above documents. 2. The appraisal procedure was legal. The China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association has a national 5A qualification for social evaluation and conducted the appraisal in accordance with relevant laws and regulations, strictly following the relevant procedures. Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's assertion that the relevant appraisal procedure was illegal lacks factual basis. (2) Qinzhou Ruifeng Company clearly knew that the first phase of the project under the contract would only yield the intermediate product of the entire project, namely titanium slag. 1. Qinzhou Ruifeng Company clearly knew that the process of the first phase of the project under the contract differed from the process recorded in the Appraisal Certificate. In the test process corresponding to the Appraisal Certificate, iron blocks were screened, resulting in higher proportions of titanium and vanadium in the product. Titanium slag was merely an intermediate product of this process, requiring further treatment to obtain high titanium slag. When Beihang University and Qinzhou Ruifeng Company planned the project under the contract, they adjusted the process for safety reasons, eliminating the above screening step. Therefore, the product obtained was titanium slag, not high titanium slag. 2. There is sufficient evidence to prove that Qinzhou Ruifeng Company clearly knew that the product of the first phase of the project under the contract was titanium slag. (1) The contract in question explicitly stipulated that the product of the first phase of the project was titanium slag, that the final product required a second phase, and that a contract for the second phase would be separately signed. (2) The "Inquiry Letter for Titanium Dioxide Engineering" submitted by Beihang University during the first instance trial of this case can also prove that Qinzhou Ruifeng Company knew that the product of the first phase of the project was only an intermediate product. (3) The "Environmental Impact Report for the Industrial Demonstration Project (Phase I) of Qinzhou Ruifeng Vanadium-Titanium-Iron Separation Technology of Qinzhou Ruifeng Vanadium-Titanium-Iron Technology Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as the "Environmental Impact Report"), prepared by Beijing Bilan Marine Environmental Protection Services Co., Ltd. commissioned by Qinzhou Ruifeng Company on May 30, 2010, and completed in September 2010, can also prove that Qinzhou Ruifeng Company knew that the product of the first phase of the project was only an intermediate product. Pages 31 to 36 of the Environmental Impact Report set forth the raw and auxiliary material composition and material balance analysis of the first phase of the project. The product obtained after reduction smelting was titanium slag containing 27.7% titanium, equivalent to a titanium dioxide content of 46.17%. (3) The First Instance Court's decision not to admit the Guangxi Transportation Company Expert Review Opinion was proper. The main purpose of the technical exchange meeting on the Qinzhou Ruifeng vanadium-titanium magnetite project organized by Guangxi Transportation Company was to finance Qinzhou Ruifeng Company. The main focus of the meeting was whether Qinzhou Ruifeng Company could guarantee ore sand resources. In fact, Qinzhou Ruifeng Company did not control ore sand resources and had not provided any ore sand from beginning to end. The purpose of Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's participation in the contract project was not for technology research and development, but to obtain benefits such as cheap government land, shareholder investment, and bank loans. As for the synthetic rutile technology recorded in the Demonstration Project Supplementary Report, this was another technology held by Beihang University and did not fall within the scope of research and development agreed upon in the contract in question. Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's decision to convene its own supplementary report revision meeting for the purpose of financing, and to include content related to synthetic rutile technology in the report, was unrelated to Beihang University. (4) The First Instance Court's determination that Beihang University's comprehensive utilization technology of vanadium-titanium magnetite sand had no fatal defects was proper; Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's claim that the comprehensive utilization technology of vanadium-titanium magnetite sand was false technology lacks support. Qinzhou Ruifeng Company had its own professional technical advisors and engineering personnel, and it had a clear understanding of Beihang University's comprehensive utilization technology of vanadium-titanium magnetite sand and the products agreed upon in the contract in question. As for Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's assertion that Beihang University falsely claimed vanadium-containing molten iron as ferrovanadium, this is a misinterpretation of Beihang University's intention. According to the text on page 1 of the Demonstration Project Application Report, dated "2009.12", it states "ferrovanadium intermetallic compound (hereinafter referred to as ferrovanadium)." This abbreviation was written by Beihang University at the request of Qinzhou Ruifeng Company. Qinzhou Ruifeng Company was aware of the meaning of "ferrovanadium" in the specific context of this case. (5) Beihang University did not falsely report technology development costs. The total contract price agreed upon by Qinzhou Ruifeng Company and Beihang University was RMB 315 million, which included Beihang University's research and development fees, labor costs, university management fees, water fees, design and manufacturing, installation and use costs of main equipment and facilities, and also included costs for the vanadium slag and iron separation processing system and subsequent technical transformation of all equipment and facilities. New Metallurgy Company only designed, constructed, and installed the basic equipment required for this research and development project based on the parameters and research and development process requirements provided by Beihang University. This did not include the vanadium slag and iron separation processing system, subsequent technical transformation of equipment and facilities, research and development, and other costs. Therefore, the contract price of RMB 170.2 million between Beihang University and New Metallurgy Company was not the total cost of the project under the contract between Beihang University and Qinzhou Ruifeng Company, and it cannot be concluded that Beihang University falsely reported RMB 144.8 million in technology development costs. In summary, Beihang University disagreed with Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's appeal requests and requested that the First Instance Judgment be affirmed.

Qinzhou Ruifeng Company filed a lawsuit with the First Instance Court, requesting: 1. Rescind the contract in question; 2. Order Beihang University to immediately return the technology development funding of RMB 57,960,000 already paid by Qinzhou Ruifeng Company; 3. Order Beihang University to compensate Qinzhou Ruifeng Company for economic losses of RMB 227,040,000; 4. Order Beihang University to bear the litigation costs of this case.

The facts found by the court of first instance: On October 8, 2008, the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association held, at Beihang University, an appraisal meeting for the scientific and technological achievement "Comprehensive Utilization Technology of Vanadium-Titanium Magnetite Sand," completed by Beijing Jinkun Hongyu Mining Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Beijing Jinkun Hongyu Company), Beihang University, and other entities. The seven experts attending the appraisal meeting were: 1. Qiu Dingfan, academician of Beijing General Research Institute of Mining and Metallurgy; 2. Zhang Guocheng, academician of Beijing General Research Institute of Nonferrous Metals; 3. Liu Guangding, academician of the Institute of Geology and Geophysics, Chinese Academy of Sciences; 4. Dong Hongchao, professor-level senior engineer at the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Technology Development and Exchange Center; 5. Ma Jilun, professor-level senior engineer at the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association; 6. Li Guoxun, professor-level senior engineer at the Beijing General Research Institute of Nonferrous Metals; 7. Cang Daqiang, professor at the University of Science and Technology Beijing. Subsequently, the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association issued a "Certificate of Appraisal," which recorded the achievement name as "Comprehensive Utilization Technology of Vanadium-Titanium Magnetite Sand," the completing units as Beijing Jinkun Hongyu Company and Beihang University, and the form of appraisal as a meeting appraisal. The "Certificate of Appraisal" mainly consisted of five parts: "Brief Technical Description and Main Performance Indicators," "Prospects for Promotion and Application and Measures," "Directory and Sources of Main Technical Documents," "Appraisal Opinion," and "Opinion of the Unit Presiding over the Appraisal." The part "Directory and Sources of Main Technical Documents" recorded: 1. Outline for appraisal of comprehensive utilization technology of vanadium-titanium magnetite sand; 2. Technical report on comprehensive utilization technology of vanadium-titanium magnetite sand; 3. Economic benefit analysis report on comprehensive utilization technology of vanadium-titanium magnetite sand; 4. Appendices: (1) Technology development contract — Beijing Jinkun Hongyu Company, Beihang University; (2) Test reports — National Steel Materials Testing Center, National Nonferrous Metals and Electronic Materials Analysis and Testing Center, Experimental Center of PetroChina Research Institute of Petroleum Exploration and Development, National Coal Quality Supervision and Testing Center, Ironmaking Engineering Technology Research Office of Central Iron and Steel Research Institute; (3) Science and technology novelty search report — Science and Technology Novelty Search Station of the Ministry of Education. The part "Appraisal Opinion" recorded: 1. The technical data provided are complete, the data are reliable, and they meet the appraisal requirements. 2. This project is the first in China to utilize coastal vanadium-titanium magnetite sand, effectively recovering iron, titanium, and vanadium, achieving comprehensive utilization of resources, which will be of great significance for alleviating the shortage of iron resources in China. Its technical characteristics and innovation points are as follows: (1) A new process of producing lump iron by direct reduction and smelting separation in a rotary hearth furnace — producing high-titanium slag by deep reduction and smelting separation in an electric furnace was adopted, with recovery rates of iron, titanium, and vanadium reaching 90%, 85%, and 85%, respectively. (2) Unique additives and catalysts were successfully developed to effectively separate lump iron from high-vanadium-titanium iron slag. (3) Further, titanium dioxide and vanadium pentoxide products were obtained from the high-vanadium-titanium iron slag through electric furnace smelting separation and hydrometallurgical technology. 3. This experiment optimized the process technical conditions, with a simple process flow and advanced technology, providing a technical basis for industrial experiments. It is expected to have good economic and social benefits, and its process technology has reached the international leading level. 4. The implementation of this project conforms to the national policies on circular economy, energy conservation, and emission reduction, and is of great significance for the resource utilization and clean treatment of difficult-to-treat vanadium-titanium magnetite and low-grade exploration ores. 5. It is recommended to carry out industrial experiments and build an industrial demonstration base for processing vanadium-titanium magnetite as soon as possible.

On March 3, 2009, Beijing Jinkun Hongyu Company and Beihang University applied for an invention patent entitled "Industrial Production Method for Directly Producing Iron and Vanadium-Titanium-Aluminum Alloy from Vanadium-Titanium Magnetite Sand," which was granted on June 15, 2011, with patent number ZL200910078765.6, the patentees being Beijing Jinkun Hongyu Company and Beihang University, and the inventor being Lu Huimin. The "Abstract" part of the patent records: The present invention discloses an industrial production method for directly producing iron and vanadium-titanium-aluminum alloy from vanadium-titanium magnetite sand. The method first pelletizes the vanadium-titanium magnetite sand obtained from nature, then subjects the pellets to drying treatment, reduction smelting separation, screening to extract lump iron, and finally uses an aluminothermic reduction method on the vanadium-titanium slag to obtain vanadium-titanium-aluminum alloy. The lump iron obtained by the production method of the present invention has a content of about 93%, and the recovery rates of iron, vanadium, and titanium are 90%, 85%, and 85%, respectively.

The "Brief Feasibility Analysis Report on the Comprehensive Utilization Project of Southeast Asian Coastal Vanadium-Titanium Magnetite Sand," formed on April 12, 2009, and signed by "Lu Huimin of Beijing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics," records in the "Significance of the Project" section: China's steel industry faces a major crisis of iron ore resources, while there are 60 billion tons of coastal vanadium-titanium magnetite sand reserves in neighboring Southeast Asian countries, which have not been utilized so far due to the lack of vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology. This project has developed a new process using vanadium-titanium magnetite sand as raw material, adopting a rotary hearth furnace direct reduction smelting separation to produce high-titanium slag, directly achieving effective separation of iron, titanium, and vanadium. The pelletizing technology with unique additives and catalysts and the rotary hearth furnace direct reduction smelting separation are the key technologies of the process; further, hydrometallurgical technology is used to produce titanium dioxide and vanadium pentoxide products, achieving comprehensive utilization of vanadium-titanium magnetite sand. The report records in the "Source of Comprehensive Utilization Technology for Vanadium-Titanium Magnetite Sand" section: Beihang University and Beijing Jinkun Hongyu Company have developed process research on direct reduction smelting separation technology for vanadium-titanium magnetite sand, metallized pellet slag-iron separation technology, deep reduction smelting slag vanadium extraction, and titanium extraction technology, and have developed a complete set of equipment for comprehensive utilization of vanadium-titanium magnetite sand, completing laboratory and semi-industrial scale tests for direct reduction smelting separation of vanadium-titanium magnetite sand, with iron, vanadium, and titanium recovery rates reaching 90%, 85%, and 85%, respectively, forming a complete set of technology and equipment for comprehensive utilization of vanadium-titanium magnetite sand with China's independent intellectual property rights. The technical characteristics of this project are: This project uses vanadium-titanium magnetite sand as raw material, adopting a new process of rotary hearth furnace direct reduction smelting separation to produce lump iron - electric furnace deep reduction to produce high-titanium slag, achieving effective separation of iron, titanium, and vanadium; the pelletizing technology with unique additives and catalysts and the rotary hearth furnace direct reduction smelting separation are the key technologies of the process; further, hydrometallurgical technology is used to produce titanium dioxide and vanadium pentoxide products. The process flow for comprehensive utilization of vanadium-titanium magnetite sand is: raw material - mixing - industrial pressing of pellets - rotary hearth furnace direct reduction smelting separation - lump iron, high-vanadium-titanium iron slag - electric furnace deep reduction smelting separation - high-titanium slag, high-vanadium slag - hydrometallurgy - vanadium pentoxide product, titanium dioxide. The report records in the "Economic Benefits and Investment" section: It is appropriate to build a 10M rotary hearth furnace, with an annual output of 100,000 tons of pig iron, processing 184,400 tons of vanadium-titanium magnetite sand, and producing by-products of 14,800 tons of titanium dioxide and 980 tons of vanadium pentoxide. The total output value of all products is RMB 557.4 million, the total production cost is RMB 224.1 million, a profit of RMB 238.542 million is realized, a net profit of RMB 178.9065 million, taxes and fees of RMB 154.3935 million, and a total profit and tax of RMB 333.3 million. Total investment is RMB 250 million, including RMB 120 million for the iron system, RMB 50 million for the titanium system, RMB 30 million for the vanadium system, RMB 30 million for working capital, RMB 20 million for initial working capital, and a construction period of 8 months.

In February 2010, Mr. Chen Keying, a representative of Hong Kong Ruifeng Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hong Kong Ruifeng Company), was introduced to Professor Lu Huimin of the School of Materials Science and Engineering of Beihang University. Professor Lu Huimin introduced to Chen Keying the world-leading short-flow rotary hearth furnace technology developed by his scientific research team, and the two parties intended to cooperate to promote the implementation of an industrial demonstration project for vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology. Subsequently, Hong Kong Ruifeng Company and Beihang University held several negotiations on the cooperation of the vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology industrial demonstration project, and Hong Kong Ruifeng Company also visited Beihang University multiple times to inspect the relevant technology. Beihang University provided Hong Kong Ruifeng Company with the "Demonstration Project Application Report" and the "Energy Conservation Special Report for the Vanadium-Titanium-Iron Separation Technology Industrial Demonstration Project," which were signed by Beihang University and Xin Ye Company. Lu Huimin was one of the two principal report preparation leaders and one of the eight report preparation personnel listed first in the above two materials. The "Demonstration Project Application Report" includes 11 aspects: 1. Application unit and project overview; 2. Strategic planning, industrial policies, and industry access; 3. Project site selection and land use; 4. Technical scheme selection, main process flow, and advancement of the technical scheme; 5. Resource development and comprehensive utilization; 6. Energy conservation scheme; 7. Environmental and ecological impact; 8. Human resources allocation and project implementation schedule; 9. Economic impact analysis; 10. Social impact analysis; 11. Research conclusions. The report is also appended with the "Certificate of Appraisal for the Comprehensive Utilization Project of Coastal Vanadium-Titanium Magnetite Sand," the "National Invention Patent Application for Vanadium-Titanium-Iron Separation from Coastal Vanadium-Titanium Magnetite Sand," the "Catalogue for Guiding Industrial Structure Adjustment (2005 Edition)," and the "Notice of the National Development and Reform Commission on Organizing the Implementation of a Major Special Project for Circular Economy High-Tech Industry (FGGBGJ [2007] No. 2289)." The "Opinions of the Evaluation Expert Group on the Energy Conservation Special Report for the Vanadium-Titanium-Iron Separation Technology Industrial Demonstration Project," formed on June 12, 2010, records: Invited by the Qinzhou Center of the Guangxi Engineering Consulting Center, the evaluation expert group for the "Energy Conservation Special Report for the Vanadium-Titanium-Iron Separation Technology Industrial Demonstration Project" consisted of three persons... "The content of this special report complies with regulatory requirements and has a certain breadth and depth." "The total energy consumption and energy structure of the project are basically reasonable. The project design adopts the world's advanced rotary hearth furnace direct reduction - electric heating melting, deep reduction smelting separation process, which is currently the most advanced process and complies with national industrial policies." "The raw materials for this project come from vanadium-titanium iron sand produced on the coast of Indonesia, fully utilizing the geographical advantages of Qinzhou, greatly reducing transportation energy consumption."

On March 30, 2010, Hong Kong Ruifeng Company, as Party A, signed a "Technology Use Contract" with Beijing Jinkun Hongyu Company as Party B, stipulating that Hong Kong Ruifeng Company would obtain the right to use the semi-industrial test technology achievements of Beijing Jinkun Hongyu Company regarding coastal vanadium-titanium magnetite sand at a price of RMB 7 million. This contract has been actually performed. In the same period, Hong Kong Ruifeng Company negotiated with the Qinzhou Municipal People's Government of Guangxi on the location of the vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology industrial demonstration project. On April 10, 2010, Hong Kong Ruifeng Company signed an agreement with the Qinzhou Municipal People's Government of Guangxi, deciding to locate the vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology industrial demonstration project in Qinzhou and to proceed with the establishment of Qinzhou Ruifeng Company. Subsequently, Qinzhou Ruifeng Company, as a wholly-owned enterprise established in Mainland China by Hong Kong Ruifeng Company as its shareholder (promoter), was established on June 24, 2011, with its business period from June 24, 2011 to June 24, 2015.

On August 10, 2010, Party A, Qinzhou Ruifeng Company, as the Client, and Party B, Beihang University, as the Contractor, signed a "Technology Development (Client) Contract" at Beihang University. The effective period of the contract is from August 10, 2010 to December 31, 2015. The contract stipulates that the parties will jointly research and develop the vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology industrial demonstration project. Chen Keying, as the legal representative of Qinzhou Ruifeng Company and the representative of Hong Kong Ruifeng Company, signed the contract, and the seals of Qinzhou Ruifeng Company and Beihang University were affixed. On August 10, 2010, Qinzhou Ruifeng Company, as Party A, and Beihang University, as Party B, also entered into the Technical Appendix to the Technical Development (Commissioned) Contract, which stipulated in Article 2 the basic process: the process adopts multiple advanced energy-saving technologies and can achieve environmentally friendly clean production; moreover, the process does not use coking coal, which is scarce in resources and expensive, thereby greatly reducing dependence on resources. The main process of coal-based rotary hearth furnace reduction is as follows: batching, mixing, balling, and drying of carbon-containing pellets are added to the hearth of a rotary hearth furnace with a rotatable bottom. During one rotation of the hearth, the pellets are reduced by carbon to obtain metallized pellets. The process plan for the project is mainly divided into three parts: the raw material pretreatment system, the pre-reduction system, and the smelting reduction and slag-iron separation system. Article 4 stipulated the equipment performance requirements: 4.1 Basic design conditions: Process: balling, drying, coal-based rotary hearth furnace pre-reduction, separation; Production capacity: annual output of 300,000 tons of pig iron; Raw materials: Indonesian coastal vanadium-titanium magnetite sand; Products: pig iron, titanium slag, and vanadium slag (titanium dioxide and vanadium pentoxide preparation will be determined by another contract); Fuel: natural gas. 4.2 Raw material pretreatment system: The raw material pretreatment system mainly adopts carbon-containing pellet balling technology. This section provides qualified pellets as furnace feed for the subsequent direct reduction. It consists of a coal crushing and grinding system, a batching system, a conveying system, a raw material mixing system, a balling system, a waste heat utilization drying system, and a dust removal system. 4.3 Rotary hearth furnace pre-reduction system: The principle of rotary hearth furnace pre-reduction is to transfer the high temperature of the burning flame through the furnace wall by radiation to the surface of the pellet layer, so that the iron ore fines in the carbon-containing pellets are reduced by the carbon and volatile matter therein at high temperatures. Its outstanding advantage is that the carbon-containing pellets are heated by open flames at high temperatures, and the reaction ends within 15-30 minutes, thus achieving rapid reduction. During the reduction process, the movement direction of the pellets is opposite to the hot gas flow after coal gas combustion, improving thermal efficiency. Since the iron oxides in the carbon-containing pellets undergo a reduction reaction with solid carbon at high temperatures, the requirements for the environmental atmosphere are not high, and the reaction speed is very fast. 4.4 Smelting deep reduction and slag-iron separation system: The reduced pellets are hot-charged into a smelting furnace for separation, obtaining reduced molten iron, vanadium slag, and titanium slag.
