The first-instance court held that Article 3 of the Supreme People's Court's "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (III)" (2014 Revision) stipulates: "Where a promoter enters into a contract externally in the name of a company being established, and after the company is established, the counterparty requests the company to assume contractual liability, the people's court shall support it. If there is evidence after the company is established that the promoter used the name of the company being established to enter into a contract for its own benefit with the counterparty, and the company refuses to assume contractual liability on this ground, the people's court shall support it, except where the counterparty is bona fide." According to this, since the promoter entered into a contract externally in the name of the company being established, the company should assume contractual liability after its establishment; similarly, after the company is established, it can also assert its rights. In this case, although the relevant "Technical Development (Commissioned) Contract" was signed when Qinzhou Ruifeng Company was still in the process of being established, after the contract was signed, Qinzhou Ruifeng Company was legally established. Moreover, the "Technical Development (Commissioned) Contract" bears the seal of Qinzhou Ruifeng Company and the signature of its legal representative. At the same time, Qinzhou Ruifeng Company does not deny the binding force of the "Technical Development (Commissioned) Contract" on it. Therefore, Qinzhou Ruifeng Company is entitled to file this lawsuit.

Article 54 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law) provides: "A party shall have the right to request a people's court or an arbitration institution to modify or rescind a contract in any of the following circumstances: (1) the contract is concluded due to a major misunderstanding; (2) the contract is obviously unfair at the time of its conclusion. If a contract is concluded by one party through fraud or duress, or by taking advantage of the other party's distress, causing the other party to express a true intention contrary to its actual intention, the injured party shall have the right to request a people's court or an arbitration institution to modify or rescind the contract. If a party requests modification, the people's court or arbitration institution shall not rescind the contract." Article 9 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Technical Contract Disputes provides: "If one party, by means of fraud, treats its existing technological achievements as the subject matter of research and development to conclude an entrusted development contract with another party and collects research and development fees, or concludes separate entrusted development contracts with two or more clients successively for the same research and development project and repeatedly collects research and development fees, and the injured party requests modification or rescission of the contract in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 54 of the Contract Law, the people's court shall support such request." Article 11 provides: "After a technical contract is invalidated or rescinded, if the developer under a technology development contract, the transferor under a technology transfer contract, or the受托人 under a technology consulting contract or a technology service contract has performed or partially performed the agreed obligations, and the fault causing the invalidation or rescission of the contract lies with the other party, the people's court may determine that the research and development funds, technology use fees, or remuneration for consulting services that should have been received for the performed part constitute losses incurred by the other party due to the invalidation or rescission of the contract. After a technical contract is invalidated or rescinded, if the parties fail to reach a new agreement on the ownership and benefit sharing of new technological achievements completed through the performance of the contract or technological achievements subsequently improved based on others' technological achievements, the people's court may rule that the party that completed the technological achievements shall enjoy such rights." In determining whether fraud exists in the process of contract formation, attention must be paid to distinguishing between legal risks and commercial risks of the contract. Legal risks of a contract refer to risks in the legal aspect of the contract, such as whether there are circumstances like fraud or duress in the contract formation process that affect the validity of the contract. Commercial risks of a contract refer to commercial risks that a lawfully effective contract may encounter during its performance, such as whether it can be smoothly performed and whether it can generate profits. Generally speaking, the Contract Law can regulate legal risks in the contract formation process but cannot regulate commercial risks in the contract performance process. In this case, Qinzhou Ruifeng Company claimed that Beihang University fraudulently induced it to enter into the "Technology Development (Entrustment) Contract." However, as early as October 8, 2008, the vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology provided by Beihang University had passed the appraisal of the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association. In its appraisal opinion, the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association pointed out the characteristics and innovations of the vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology, stating: "This project is the first in China to utilize coastal vanadium-titanium magnetite sand to effectively recover iron, titanium, and vanadium, achieving comprehensive utilization of resources, which is of great significance for alleviating China's iron resource shortage. … Its process technology has reached the international leading level"; "The implementation of this project complies with the national circular economy and energy-saving and emission reduction policies, and is of great significance for the resource utilization and cleaning of difficult-to-process vanadium-titanium magnetite and low-grade exploration resources"; and it recommended "conducting industrial tests as soon as possible and establishing an industrial demonstration base for processing vanadium-titanium magnetite." During the process of signing the "Technology Development (Entrustment) Contract," relevant personnel of Beihang University and Qinzhou Ruifeng Company had multiple contacts and repeated consultations, and relevant personnel of Qinzhou Ruifeng Company also visited Beihang University multiple times to inspect related technical issues. Although the "Expert Review Opinion of Guangxi Communications Company," formed at the technology exchange meeting for the Qinzhou Ruifeng vanadium-titanium magnetite project organized by Guangxi Communications Industry Co., Ltd. on July 26, 2013, pointed out certain possible defects in the "Vanadium-Titanium Separation Technology Industrialization Demonstration Project" under the "Technology Development (Entrustment) Contract," and Qinzhou Ruifeng Company accordingly claimed that the technology provided by Beihang University was unworkable and thus constituted fraud, the court of first instance found upon examination that this claim by Qinzhou Ruifeng Company could not be established. This is because the technology exchange meeting for the Qinzhou Ruifeng vanadium-titanium magnetite project held on July 26, 2013, was organized by Guangxi Communications Industry Co., Ltd. when difficulties arose during the performance of the "Technology Development (Entrustment) Contract." Its nature was a technology exchange meeting rather than a technology appraisal meeting. It focused more on problems that emerged during the performance of the "Technology Development (Entrustment) Contract" rather than problems inherent in the technology provided by Beihang University. Its appraisal target was mainly whether the "Vanadium-Titanium Separation Technology Industrialization Demonstration Project" was feasible rather than whether the technology provided by Beihang University had fatal defects. Its purpose was to help Guangxi Communications Industry Co., Ltd. decide whether to invest in and become a shareholder of the "Vanadium-Titanium Separation Technology Industrialization Demonstration Project." The meeting materials seen by the participants were also different from the meeting materials used when the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association conducted the appraisal of the vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology on October 8, 2008. That is, the organizer of this exchange meeting had a direct interest in the relevant conclusions. Therefore, the expert review opinion formed after this exchange meeting was insufficient to negate the authoritative appraisal conclusion of the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association on October 8, 2008, regarding the vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology. Accordingly, based solely on the technology exchange meeting for the Qinzhou Ruifeng vanadium-titanium magnetite project organized by Guangxi Communications Industry Co., Ltd. on July 26, 2013, and the resulting "Expert Review Opinion of Guangxi Communications Company," it was insufficient to determine that the technology provided by Beihang University under the "Technology Development (Entrustment) Contract" had fatal defects. At the same time, the transition from successful research and development in the laboratory to industrial application is a difficult process. Even for successfully developed technologies, encountering some problems during the industrialization transformation process is normal, and it requires sincere cooperation between the contracting parties rather than mutual obstruction. Although obstacles in the industrialization process of the relevant technology may be due to defects in the technology itself, this requires sufficient and valid evidence to prove. In the absence of sufficient and effective evidence, it cannot be deduced that the technology itself necessarily has fatal defects simply because obstacles were encountered during its industrialization. Therefore, in the absence of sufficient and effective evidence proving that the technology provided by Beihang University had fatal defects, the court of first instance found that Beihang University did not commit fraud in cooperating with Qinzhou Ruifeng Company to sign the "Technology Development (Entrustment) Contract" using its appraised and qualified vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology to seek industrialization. Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's claim based on Beihang University's fraud to rescind the "Technology Development (Entrustment) Contract" numbered Qin Rui Jian-001 and related appendices signed on August 10, 2010, and its request for Beihang University to return the technology development funds already paid and compensate for its economic losses lacked sufficient basis. The court of first instance did not support it.

Article 55 of the Contract Law provides: "The right to rescind shall be extinguished under any of the following circumstances: (1) a party having the right to rescind fails to exercise such right within one year from the date on which it knew or should have known the grounds for rescission; (2) a party having the right to rescind, after knowing the grounds for rescission, expressly indicates or by its own conduct waives the right to rescind." Article 7 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Statute of Limitations System in the Trial of Civil Cases provides: "If a party entitled to the right to rescind requests rescission of a contract, the one-year limitation period provided in Article 55 of the Contract Law shall apply. If the other party raises a statute of limitations defense against the claim for rescission of the contract, the people's court shall not support it. After the contract is rescinded, the statute of limitations for the claim for return of property and compensation for losses shall commence from the date of rescission." Article 8 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (I) provides: "The 'one year' provided in Article 55, and the 'five years' provided in Articles 75 and 104, paragraph 2, of the Contract Law are unchangeable periods and are not subject to suspension, interruption, or extension of the statute of limitations." Whether fraud exists in the process of contract formation should not be based solely on a party's speculation but should be supported by certain evidence. That is, only on the basis of certain evidence can it be determined that a party knew or should have known the fraudulent situation. In this case, although the relevant technology contract was signed on August 10, 2010, Qinzhou Ruifeng Company stated that after the expert review opinion from the technology exchange meeting for the Qinzhou Ruifeng vanadium-titanium magnetite project organized by Guangxi Communications Industry Co., Ltd. on August 1, 2013, raised questions about Beihang University's technology, it only then became aware of the alleged "fraud" and filed the lawsuit. Beihang University also failed to provide effective evidence to prove that Qinzhou Ruifeng Company had known of the alleged "fraud" earlier. Accordingly, the court of first instance found that Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's filing of this lawsuit in July 2014 had not exceeded the one-year period provided in Article 55 of the Contract Law. Beihang University's defense that the lawsuit filed by Qinzhou Ruifeng Company had exceeded the statutory period could not be established, and the court of first instance did not support it.

In conclusion, the court of first instance rendered the following judgment: All claims of Qinzhou Ruifeng Company were dismissed.

During the second instance of this court, the parties submitted evidence in accordance with the law regarding their appeal requests. This court organized the parties to exchange and cross-examine the evidence. Qinzhou Ruifeng Company submitted the following four pieces of evidence: Evidence 1, "Material Balance Calculation Report," intended to prove that using the mineral sand as stated in the "Demonstration Project Application Report" and the "Supplementary Report on the Demonstration Project" as raw materials, and utilizing the vanadium-titanium iron ore comprehensive utilization technology recorded in the "Appraisal Certificate," it is impossible to produce high-vanadium iron water and high-titanium slag with a titanium dioxide content of 87.29%, but only low-value vanadium-containing iron water and molten titanium slag with a titanium dioxide content of approximately 45%. Evidence 2, the "Analysis Technical Consultation Report on the 'Vanadium-Titanium Magnetite Sand Comprehensive Utilization Process' of the School of Materials Science and Engineering, Beihang University" (referred to as the "Aowo Company Consultation Report") prepared by Tianjin Aowo Metallurgical Technology Consulting Co., Ltd. (referred to as Aowo Company), intended to prove: (1) The rotary hearth furnace does not have the function of melting and reducing iron, nor can it melt the reduced iron and separate the solution into "block iron" and "high-vanadium-titanium-iron slag"; (2) Using Beihang University's vanadium-titanium magnetite sand comprehensive utilization technology, with the mineral sand of the composition recorded in the relevant materials as raw materials, it is impossible to produce high-vanadium iron water and high-titanium slag, but only vanadium-containing iron water and molten titanium slag with a titanium dioxide content of 45-50%. Evidence 3, the defense opinion submitted by Beihang University during the first instance of this case, intended to prove that Beihang University admitted to technology fraud. The technical characteristics and innovations recognized at the scientific and technological achievements appraisal meeting organized by the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association on Beihang University's vanadium-titanium magnetite sand comprehensive utilization technology, as stated in Beihang University's first-instance defense opinion, were completely different from the technical characteristics and innovations recorded in the "Appraisal Certificate" issued after that meeting. Beihang University stated in its defense petition that the meeting recognized its technical characteristics and innovations as "using a rotary hearth furnace for pre-reduction" and "using an electric furnace for deep reduction and molten separation technology to achieve effective separation of vanadium-containing iron water and titanium slag," whereas the "Appraisal Certificate" recorded the technical characteristics and innovations as "rotary hearth furnace reduction and molten separation" and "electric furnace deep reduction and molten separation to produce high-titanium slag new process." Evidence 4, the "Measures for the Appraisal of Scientific and Technological Achievements" of the State Science and Technology Commission and Announcement No. 1 of 2011 of the Ministry of Science and Technology, intended to prove that the appraisal conducted by the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association on Beihang University's vanadium-titanium magnetite sand comprehensive utilization technology did not comply with the relevant provisions of the "Measures for the Appraisal of Scientific and Technological Achievements." Article 10, paragraph 2 of the "Measures for the Appraisal of Scientific and Technological Achievements" provides: "Conference appraisal: refers to the evaluation of scientific and technological achievements by peer experts in the form of a conference. For scientific and technological achievements that require on-site inspection, testing, and discussion and debate to be evaluated, the conference appraisal form may be used." The record in the "Test Report of the Appraisal Committee" section of the "Appraisal Certificate" is "None," and the date of appraisal and the date of approval of the appraisal recorded on the cover of the "Appraisal Certificate" are only one day apart. It can be seen that the appraisal in this case did not undergo on-site inspection and testing, and the "Appraisal Certificate" is not legally valid.

Beihang University expressed cross-examination opinions on the above four pieces of evidence, considering: 1. Evidence 1 is not new evidence, is not stamped, and lacks authenticity, legality, and relevance. 2. Evidence 2 existed before the first-instance trial and should have been submitted during the first instance, so it does not constitute new evidence for the second instance. This report has no entrusting party, the reporting unit Aowo Company does not have the qualification for appraising technological achievements, some of the report's authors have an interest relationship with Qinzhou Ruifeng Company, and the report's authors evaluated the technology based on imagination without seeing the relevant technical materials of Beihang University's vanadium-titanium magnetite sand comprehensive utilization technology. According to existing technology, block iron can appear at 1400-1450 degrees, so the report's claim that melting requires 1800 degrees is incorrect. 3. Evidence 3 itself does not constitute evidence and cannot prove the facts to be proven. Moreover, this defense opinion was submitted by Beihang University before the first-instance trial. After trial cross-examination and debate, Beihang University's position has changed and should no longer be taken as accurate. 4. Evidence 4 itself also does not constitute evidence and cannot prove the facts to be proven. Moreover, the appraisal of Beihang University's vanadium-titanium magnetite sand comprehensive utilization technology included both testing appraisal and conference appraisal. Before the conference appraisal, the products from the two-meter furnace test had already been submitted for testing by a state-designated testing institution, and there were corresponding test results and reports. There are relevant provisions on when on-site testing is required. The vanadium-titanium magnetite sand comprehensive utilization technology cannot be tested on-site, and the appraisal by the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association did not violate procedures.

Beihang University also submitted two sets of evidence during the second instance of this case: 1. The first set of evidence, the "Environmental Impact Assessment Report" and its Entrustment Letter, intended to prove: (1) Before signing the "Technology Development (Entrustment) Contract" with Beihang University, Qinzhou Ruifeng Company had, on May 30, 2010, entrusted Beijing Bilan Marine Environmental Protection Service Co., Ltd. to prepare an environmental impact report for the "Vanadium-Titanium-Iron Separation Industrial Demonstration Project (Phase I)." Therefore, Qinzhou Ruifeng Company was aware that only Phase I was being developed first and that this phase could not produce the final product. (2) According to the content on pages 32 to 35 of the "Environmental Impact Assessment Report," Qinzhou Ruifeng Company did not provide the mineral sand raw materials required for Phase I; it used the mineral sand raw material data of Jinkun Hongyu Company, and it was aware that the product of Phase I would be titanium slag. 2. The second set of evidence, an untrue report about this case published in the "Law and Life" magazine, a letter from Beihang University to the "Law and Life" magazine and the courier receipt for sending that letter, and a statement from the "Law and Life" magazine, intended to prove that Qinzhou Ruifeng Company released false information and maliciously interfered with the litigation.

Qinzhou Ruifeng Company expressed cross-examination opinions on the above two sets of evidence, considering: 1. The first set of evidence cannot prove the facts to be proven. The environmental assessment was based on data provided by Beihang University, and the relevant assessment matters were also negotiated by Beihang University, having nothing to do with Qinzhou Ruifeng Company. Moreover, Qinzhou Ruifeng Company received the "Environmental Impact Assessment Report" only after the signing of the "Technology Development (Entrustment) Contract," so the report cannot explain the situation before the contract was signed. 2. The second set of evidence also cannot prove the facts to be proven. There is currently no evidence proving that Qinzhou Ruifeng Company colluded with the "Law and Life" magazine. The article published by that magazine has nothing to do with Qinzhou Ruifeng Company.

Regarding the above evidence of Qinzhou Ruifeng Company and Beihang University, this court certifies as follows: Evidence 1 and Evidence 4 of Qinzhou Ruifeng Company, in nature, do not constitute civil litigation evidence as defined in Article 63 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Beihang University's second set of evidence is obviously not relevant to the determination of facts in this case. Therefore, Evidence 1 and Evidence 4 of Qinzhou Ruifeng Company and Beihang University's second set of evidence need not be further commented on. As for whether Evidence 2 and Evidence 3 submitted by Qinzhou Ruifeng Company can prove the facts to be proven, this involves the determination of whether the vanadium-titanium magnetite sand comprehensive utilization technology is false. Whether Beihang University's first set of evidence can prove the facts to be proven involves the determination of whether Qinzhou Ruifeng Company knew that Phase I of the contract project would only produce intermediate products. This court will make a comprehensive determination in the reasoning part of the judgment, together with other relevant facts and evidence in this case.

This court finds upon further trial that the facts found by the court of first instance are true, and this court confirms them. This court additionally finds:

1. During the trial of the second instance, Beihang University presented in court six documents, including the "Vanadium-Titanium Magnetite Sand Comprehensive Utilization Technology Appraisal Outline," "Vanadium-Titanium Magnetite Sand Comprehensive Utilization Technology Report," "Vanadium-Titanium Magnetite Sand Comprehensive Utilization Technology Economic Benefit Analysis Report," "Technology Development Contract," "Test Report," and "Science and Technology Novelty Search Report." These six documents correspond to the document names recorded in the "List of Main Technical Documents and Sources" in the "Appraisal Certificate."

2. Before the signing of the contract at issue, Beihang University provided Qinzhou Ruifeng Company with two copies of the "Demonstration Project Application Report" to explain the planning of the vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology industrialization demonstration project. The contents of the two reports are basically the same, with their dates being "2010.5" and "2009.12" respectively. Qinzhou Ruifeng Company claimed that the report dated "2009.12" was actually submitted later, and Beihang University did not object to this. Therefore, the text of the "Demonstration Project Application Report" shall be based on the "2009.12" version.

This court is of the opinion, based on the first-instance judgment of this case and the reasons for appeal of Qinzhou Ruifeng Company, that the main issue in dispute in this case is: whether Qinzhou Ruifeng Company can, in accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 54 of the Contract Law, rescind the "Technology Development (Entrustment) Contract" and its technical appendices, "Contract Appendix (1)," "Contract Appendix (2)," and "Supplementary Technical Appendix" (collectively referred to as the contracts at issue) that it signed with Beihang University.

Paragraph 2 of Article 54 of the Contract Law provides that a contract concluded by a party through fraud, coercion, or exploitation of the other party's hardship, causing the other party to act contrary to its true intent, the aggrieved party has the right to request a people's court or an arbitration institution to modify or rescind the contract. This court holds that the reason a contract concluded under fraud, thus contrary to one's true intent, can be modified or rescinded is that the formation of such a contract violates the principle of autonomy of will. Autonomy of will means, on one hand, that civil subjects have the right to freely create, modify, and terminate civil legal relationships within the scope prescribed by law according to their own will; on the other hand, it also means that they must bear responsibility for their actions in creating, modifying, and terminating civil legal relationships. However, "responsibility" must be premised on and limited to "true intent"; a civil subject should not bear responsibility for a declaration of intent that is not its true intent or exceeds the scope of its true intent. Therefore, to determine whether a contract is one concluded under fraud as stipulated in Paragraph 2 of Article 54 of the Contract Law, it is necessary to examine both whether the alleged defrauding party engaged in fraudulent conduct and whether the party claiming to have been defrauded fell into a mistaken judgment due to the fraud and, based on that mistaken judgment, made a declaration of intent contrary to its true intent—both elements are indispensable. If the alleged defrauding party did not engage in fraudulent conduct at all, the contract naturally cannot be modified or rescinded on grounds of fraud. But even if the alleged defrauding party engaged in fraudulent conduct, as long as the other party did not fall into a mistaken judgment due to the fraud and its declaration of intent still conforms to its true intent, then the formation of the contract does not violate the principle of autonomy of will, and the contract cannot be modified or rescinded on that ground. Therefore, in this case, determining whether the contract in question constitutes one concluded by a party through fraud, causing the other party to act contrary to its true intent, must be analyzed from two aspects: first, whether Beihang University engaged in fraudulent conduct; second, whether Qinzhou Ruifeng Company fell into a mistaken judgment due to the fraud and, on that basis, made a declaration of intent contrary to its true intent.

(I) On the issue of whether Beihang University engaged in fraudulent conduct

According to Article 68 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), where a party intentionally informs the other party of false circumstances, or intentionally conceals the true circumstances, thereby inducing the other party to make an erroneous declaration of intent, it may be deemed as fraudulent conduct. In the field of technology entrustment development contracts, the determination of whether the受托方 (entrusted party) informed of false circumstances or concealed true circumstances must fully consider the characteristics of technology development activities themselves. Technology development activities are phased, and their outcomes are uncertain. From laboratory testing, to semi-industrial testing, industrial testing, and then to mature industrial production, the progressive advancement of research and development stages is not merely a simple increase in output and scale, but a complex process of continuously overcoming both known and unknown difficulties. Some difficulties in technology development activities may be difficult to foresee, prevent, control, or overcome. Success at each research and development stage only provides basic conditions for subsequent research and development; whether the next research and development stage will also succeed, or even whether the technological achievement will ultimately be obtained, cannot be known with certainty. Therefore, in determining fraudulent conduct by the entrusted party in a technology entrustment development contract, it is necessary to respect the characteristics and laws of technology development activities themselves, distinguish between different stages of technology development, and use the known facts at the time of contract signing and the circumstances that the entrusted party could reasonably have foreseen at that time as the standard for determining whether it informed of false circumstances or concealed true circumstances.

In this case, the contract in question is a technology development contract concerning the large-scale industrial testing stage of the comprehensive utilization technology for vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore. The preceding research and development stage involved is the semi-industrial testing stage of this technology. The determination of whether Beihang University informed Qinzhou Ruifeng Company of false circumstances or concealed true circumstances mainly involves two aspects: first, whether Beihang University fully informed Qinzhou Ruifeng Company of the true circumstances of the comprehensive utilization technology for vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore at the semi-industrial testing stage; second, whether Beihang University fully informed Qinzhou Ruifeng Company of the true plan for the industrial demonstration project for vanadium-titanium iron separation technology.

1. On the issue of whether Beihang University fully informed Qinzhou Ruifeng Company of the true circumstances of the comprehensive utilization technology for vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore at the semi-industrial testing stage

During the negotiation stage of the contract in question, Beihang University provided Hong Kong Ruifeng Company and Qinzhou Ruifeng Company with the "Appraisal Certificate" issued by the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association, to explain the relevant circumstances of the semi-industrial testing stage of the comprehensive utilization technology for vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore. This "Appraisal Certificate" was issued by the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association on October 8, 2008, after holding a scientific and technological achievement appraisal meeting at Beihang University. The seven experts participating in this appraisal included three academicians, three professor-level senior engineers, and one professor in this technical field. The "Appraisal Certificate" recorded the brief technical description, main technical performance indicators, prospects for promotion and application and measures, list and sources of main technical documents, appraisal opinions, and other content of the comprehensive utilization technology for vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore in question. The "Appraisal Opinions" section stated: "...This test optimized the process technical conditions, the process is simple, the technology is advanced, providing a technical basis for industrial testing. It is expected to have good economic and social benefits, and its process technology has reached the international advanced level. ...The implementation of this project conforms to the national industrial policy of circular economy and energy saving and emission reduction... It is recommended to carry out industrial testing as soon as possible and build an industrial demonstration base for processing vanadium-titanium magnetite." This court holds that, considering the organizing unit, appraisal personnel, appraisal process, appraisal basis, etc., of this appraisal, it should be determined that the "Appraisal Certificate" can completely and truthfully reflect the circumstances of the semi-industrial testing stage of the comprehensive utilization technology for vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore, and its appraisal opinions should be adopted. Beihang University, by providing this "Appraisal Certificate" to Hong Kong Ruifeng Company and Qinzhou Ruifeng Company during the contract negotiation stage, had fully informed them of the true circumstances regarding the semi-industrial testing stage of the comprehensive utilization technology for vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore in question. Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's claim that the above "Appraisal Certificate" should not be relied upon and that the comprehensive utilization technology for vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore in question has fatal defects lacks basis and should not be supported. The specific reasons are as follows:

(1) The basic documents and materials for this appraisal were complete

Qinzhou Ruifeng Company claimed that it obtained all archives of this appraisal from the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association, but the six documents listed in the "List of Main Technical Documents and Sources" section of the "Appraisal Certificate," including the "Appraisal Outline for the Comprehensive Utilization Technology of Vanadium-Titanium Magnetite Sand Ore," were not present. Therefore, it should be determined that this appraisal lacked basic documents and materials, and the "Appraisal Certificate" should not be relied upon. This court holds that whether the above six documents exist in the appraisal archives of the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association is a matter of whether the Association's appraisal document archiving work was proper. Considering the fact that Qinzhou Ruifeng Company did not apply within the legal limitation period to request Beihang University to produce the relevant documents, and that Beihang University had produced the above six documents in court during the second instance of this case, this court holds that the issue of whether the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association properly archived the above six documents is no longer sufficient to affect the determination of whether the basic documents and materials for this appraisal were complete. Based on the existing evidence and the facts already ascertained, it can be determined that the basic documents and materials for this appraisal were complete. Therefore, Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's claim in this regard lacks basis, and this court does not support it.

(2) The appraisal procedure was lawful

Qinzhou Ruifeng Company claimed that the appraisal committee did not test the key links of the technology in question, violating the relevant provisions of the "Measures for the Appraisal of Scientific and Technological Achievements." Therefore, it should be determined that the appraisal procedure was illegal, and the "Appraisal Certificate" should not be relied upon. This court holds that, with reference to Article 10 of the "Measures for the Appraisal of Scientific and Technological Achievements" issued by the State Science and Technology Commission, the organizing unit and presiding unit for appraisal may choose different appraisal forms, including testing appraisal, meeting appraisal, and correspondence appraisal, based on the characteristics of the scientific and technological achievement. Among them, meeting appraisal refers to evaluation of a scientific and technological achievement by peer experts in the form of a meeting. For scientific and technological achievements that require on-site inspection, testing, and discussion and defense for evaluation, the meeting appraisal form may be adopted. This provision is not a mandatory norm, let alone a validity-affecting mandatory norm. Therefore, the form of appraisal adopted for the appraisal in question does not necessarily affect the validity of the appraisal conclusion. Moreover, according to the record in the "List of Main Technical Documents and Sources" section of the appraisal certificate, Beihang University submitted "Test Reports" issued by the National Iron and Steel Materials Testing Center, the National Nonferrous Metals and Electronic Materials Analysis and Testing Center, the Experimental Center of the China Petroleum Exploration and Development Research Institute, the National Coal Quality Supervision and Testing Center, and the Ironmaking Engineering Technology Research Office of the Central Iron and Steel Research Institute to the appraisal committee. On the basis of studying the "Test Reports" and other technical materials, the appraisal committee held a meeting to discuss and defend the relevant issues of the technology in question, and then issued appraisal opinions, which complies with the provisions of the "Measures for the Appraisal of Scientific and Technological Achievements" regarding meeting appraisal. There is no circumstance of illegal appraisal procedure. Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's claim in this regard lacks basis, and this court does not support it.

(3) The "Application Report for the Demonstration Project" and Beihang University's own statements cannot overturn the "Appraisal Certificate"

Qinzhou Ruifeng Company claimed that the "Appraisal Certificate" records that the product after deep reduction smelting separation in an electric furnace is high-titanium slag with a TiO2 content of 87.29%. However, according to the law of conservation of mass, using the data recorded in the "Application Report for the Demonstration Project" to calculate, the project can only obtain titanium slag with a TiO2 content of 46.4%. Moreover, Beihang University also acknowledged in the "Supplementary Report for the Demonstration Project" and during the first instance trial that the product after electric furnace smelting separation in the industrial demonstration project for vanadium-titanium iron separation technology is titanium slag. Given that Beihang University has denied the "Appraisal Certificate" through the "Application Report for the Demonstration Project" and its own statements, and that the comprehensive utilization technology for vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore recorded in the "Appraisal Certificate" cannot obtain high-titanium slag through reduction smelting separation, the "Appraisal Certificate" should not be relied upon, and it should be determined that the comprehensive utilization technology for vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore has fatal defects. This court holds that large-scale industrial testing is not a simple reproduction of semi-industrial testing. The two differ in terms of test purpose, test environment, test scale, test equipment, etc., and the technical difficulties that may be encountered are also not entirely consistent. Adapting and improving the processes in semi-industrial testing for the purpose of smooth large-scale industrial production is exactly the intended meaning of industrial testing. Therefore, it is normal for industrial testing to differ from the processes and procedures of semi-industrial testing in terms of overall technology and specific steps. In this case, the "Appraisal Certificate" is an appraisal conclusion for the comprehensive utilization technology of vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore at the semi-industrial testing stage. Page 1 of the certificate, Section "2.1 Process Flow for Comprehensive Utilization of Vanadium-Titanium Magnetite Sand Ore," records: "...Electric furnace deep reduction smelting separation - high vanadium iron, high titanium slag..." The "Application Report for the Demonstration Project" is a project plan for the large-scale industrial testing stage of this technology. Page 21 of the report records that in the industrial testing stage, "the smelting separation process only performs titanium slag and vanadium iron separation," and the obtained titanium slag requires "further extraction and processing" to obtain high-titanium slag. It can be seen that Beihang University, based on the semi-industrial testing of the comprehensive utilization technology for vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore, made adjustments to the processes in the industrial testing stage. Page 42 of the "Application Report for the Demonstration Project" does not conceal that the TiO2 content in the titanium slag is 46%. This process adjustment is precisely the reason for the differences in descriptions of products and data between the "Application Report for the Demonstration Project," Beihang University's statements, and the "Appraisal Certificate." Therefore, this court holds that although the "Application Report for the Demonstration Project" and Beihang University's statements differ from the "Appraisal Certificate," they are not contradictory. The "Application Report for the Demonstration Project" and Beihang University's own statements do not constitute a basis for overturning the "Appraisal Certificate," nor are they sufficient to falsify the comprehensive utilization technology for vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore. Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's claim in this regard lacks basis, and this court does not support it.

(4) The "Supplementary Report for the Demonstration Project" and the "Review Opinion of the Nonferrous Metals Association" cannot overturn the "Appraisal Certificate"

Qinzhou Ruifeng Company claimed that the "Review Opinion of the Nonferrous Metals Association" issued by the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association affirmed the content of the "Supplementary Report for the Demonstration Project," while the "Supplementary Report for the Demonstration Project" denied the content of the "Appraisal Certificate" and the "Application Report for the Demonstration Project." Therefore, the "Review Opinion of the Nonferrous Metals Association" also constitutes a denial of the "Appraisal Certificate." Given that some of the experts who issued the "Review Opinion of the Nonferrous Metals Association" and the "Appraisal Certificate" are the same, it should be determined that the "Appraisal Certificate" has been overturned by its own appraisal personnel and should no longer be relied upon. This court holds that although the projects recorded in the "Application Report for the Demonstration Project" and the "Supplementary Report for the Demonstration Project" both involve the comprehensive utilization of vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore, the relevant main technologies, project products, etc., are not the same. That is, the two involve different methods for the comprehensive utilization of vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore, and they are not contradictory. Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's claim that the "Review Opinion of the Nonferrous Metals Association" and the "Supplementary Report for the Demonstration Project" denied the "Application Report for the Demonstration Project" and the "Appraisal Certificate," and therefore the "Appraisal Certificate" should not be relied upon, lacks basis. This court does not support it.

(5) The "Expert Review Opinion of Guangxi Transportation Company" cannot overturn the "Appraisal Certificate"

According to the statements of Qinzhou Ruifeng Company in its appeal opinion, the "Expert Review Opinion of Guangxi Transportation Company" is a review opinion on the artificial rutile production technology involved in the "Supplementary Report for the Demonstration Project." It is unrelated to the "Appraisal Certificate," and the participating experts did not see the "Appraisal Certificate." This court holds that precisely because the technology involved in the "Expert Review Opinion of Guangxi Transportation Company" is different from that in the "Appraisal Certificate," and the experts participating in the Guangxi Transportation Company technical exchange meeting did not study the complete technical materials under the "Appraisal Certificate," this review opinion is insufficient to falsify the comprehensive utilization technology for vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore recorded in the "Appraisal Certificate." The first instance court, comprehensively considering factors such as the background, nature, topics, objects, purpose, and materials of the technical exchange meeting organized by Guangxi Transportation Company on July 23, 2013, determined that the "Expert Review Opinion of Guangxi Transportation Company" is insufficient to overturn the "Appraisal Certificate." This was not improper, and this court affirms it.

(6) The "Consulting Report of Aowo Company" cannot overturn the "Appraisal Certificate"

During the second instance of this case, Qinzhou Ruifeng Company submitted the "Consulting Report of Aowo Company," intending to prove that the comprehensive utilization technology for vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore recorded in the "Appraisal Certificate" is false technology. Regardless of whether Aowo Company has relevant technical appraisal qualifications, according to the record of this report and the facts already ascertained, Aowo Company made the above report without referring to the relevant basic documents and materials and without asking Beihang University about the relevant technical facts. Therefore, this court does not rely on this report. This court holds that the "Consulting Report of Aowo Company" cannot overturn the "Appraisal Certificate" and cannot prove that the technology recorded in that certificate is false technology.

In summary, Beihang University fully informed Qinzhou Ruifeng Company of the true circumstances of the comprehensive utilization technology for vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore at the semi-industrial testing stage. It did not commit fraud regarding the circumstances of the technology in question at this research and development stage. Moreover, based on the existing evidence, it is difficult to determine that the comprehensive utilization technology for vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore recorded in the "Appraisal Certificate" is false technology. The first instance court's reliance on the "Appraisal Certificate" and its decision not to support Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's application for a new appraisal were not improper, and this court affirms them. Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's claim that Beihang University obtained the "Appraisal Certificate" through false technology and that the "Appraisal Certificate" should not be relied upon lacks basis, and this court does not support it.

2. On the issue of whether Beihang University fully informed Qinzhou Ruifeng Company of the true plan for the industrial demonstration project for vanadium-titanium iron separation technology

During the negotiation stage of the contract in question, Beihang University submitted the "Application Report for the Demonstration Project" to Qinzhou Ruifeng Company to explain its plan for the industrial testing project of the comprehensive utilization technology for vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore. The issue of whether Beihang University fully informed Qinzhou Ruifeng Company of the true plan for the large-scale industrial testing stage of the comprehensive utilization technology for vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore should mainly be examined from two aspects: whether Beihang University misrepresented the project products and whether it misrepresented the technology development costs.

(1) On the issue of whether Beihang University misrepresented the project products

The "Application Report for the Demonstration Project" indeed uses multiple concepts such as "titanium-rich slag," "high-titanium slag," "titanium slag," "vanadium-iron intermetallic compound," and "vanadium iron." For example: 1. Page 1 of the report states, "The project... will ultimately obtain titanium-rich slag, titanium dioxide, titanium and titanium alloys, vanadium-iron intermetallic compounds (hereinafter referred to as vanadium iron), vanadium pentoxide, and vanadium deep-processed products." 2. Page 6 of the report states, "The proposed project is to use Southeast Asian vanadium-titanium magnetite sand as raw material to produce vanadium-iron intermetallic compounds, high-titanium slag, and vanadium products urgently needed in China." 3. Page 21 of the report states, "The rotary hearth furnace direct reduction technology - molten deep reduction smelting separation process adopted in the first phase of this project is a solid reduction - non-slagging molten titanium slag and vanadium iron separation process technology. During the reduction process,... this process only achieves the reduction of iron oxides, and the intermediate product is vanadium-iron intermetallic compounds and titanium-rich vanadium-rich slag. The smelting separation process only performs titanium slag and vanadium iron separation,... titanium exists in the form of simple oxides, and further extraction and processing will be very easy. The products are high-titanium slag, vanadium-iron intermetallic compounds, and crude vanadium slag..." 4. Page 22 of the report records that the products after slag-iron separation in the rotary hearth furnace direct reduction process are titanium slag and vanadium iron. 5. Page 28 of the report states, "The main function of the smelting separation furnace is to separate the titanium slag and vanadium iron from the metallized pellets. Its products are liquid vanadium-iron intermetallic compounds and titanium slag." 6. Page 33 of the report states, "This project is the world's first to use coastal vanadium-titanium magnetite sand as raw material, adopting rotary hearth furnace direct reduction smelting separation - electric furnace deep reduction smelting separation and wet process technology to directly manufacture vanadium-iron intermetallic compounds, high-titanium slag, titanium dioxide, and vanadium pentoxide products." 7. Page 42 of the report records, "Calculation basis: Production scale: 300,000 tons of vanadium-containing iron, composition: TFe 94%, V 0.67%; 137,500 tons of titanium slag, composition: TiO2 46% (product grade in this section, raw material for the next section)."

Opinion of the Court

As discussed above, technological research and development activities are phased, with each subsequent phase not being a simple replication or scale-up of the preceding phase. Products at different R&D phases may differ. Even within the same R&D phase, different processes will correspond to different products. The so-called "intermediate product" is not a concept with a fixed reference; what constitutes an intermediate product depends on the specific process to which it corresponds. Therefore, in understanding products, particularly intermediate products, consideration must be given both to the R&D phase in which they are situated and to the specific process to which they correspond. In this case, the Application Report for the Demonstration Project includes both a review of the semi-industrial test phase of the vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore comprehensive utilization technology recorded in the Appraisal Certificate, and a project plan for the large-scale industrial test phase of that technology. It also includes both an introduction to the first phase of the demonstration project for vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology, and a prospectus for later phases. Consequently, the products referenced in the report are relatively complex. The understanding of product concepts such as "titanium-enriched slag," "high-titanium slag," "titanium slag," "ferrovanadium intermetallic compound," and "ferrovanadium" in the Application Report for the Demonstration Project must be contextualized by clarifying the R&D phase and specific process to which they refer. It is impermissible to simply conclude that the simultaneous appearance of these concepts in the report constitutes self-contradiction or a false statement. The court finds as follows: First, in the Application Report for the Demonstration Project, "titanium-enriched slag" and "high-titanium slag" generally refer to the vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore comprehensive utilization technology at the semi-industrial test phase, or to the entire industrialization demonstration project for vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology, as shown in examples 1, 2, and 6 above. Second, in the report, "titanium slag" generally refers to the first phase of the industrialization demonstration project for vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology, as shown in examples 4, 5, and 7 above. Third, according to the record on page 1 of the Application Report for the Demonstration Project, "ferrovanadium" in that report is an abbreviation for "ferrovanadium intermetallic compound." Therefore, in the context of that report, there is no difference between "ferrovanadium intermetallic compound" and "ferrovanadium." Finally, the product descriptions in the Application Report for the Demonstration Project are indeed not entirely precise. For instance, in example 3 above, concepts such as titanium slag, titanium-enriched and vanadium-enriched slag, and high-titanium slag are mixed. However, considering that: on the one hand, the concept of "intermediate product" does have a certain degree of uncertainty, and a single process flow comprising several different processes can naturally have multiple different intermediate products; on the other hand, the report's statement that the product after smelting separation is titanium slag, with a titanium dioxide content of 46%, has been clear and consistent throughout. Moreover, this is consistent with the explicit agreement in the contract in question that the products of the first phase of the industrialization demonstration project for vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology are reduced iron, titanium slag, and vanadium slag. Therefore, the court finds that the statement in example 3 above does not involve circumstances of false statements such as intentionally providing false information or intentionally concealing the true situation.

In summary, the court finds that the statements regarding products in the Application Report for the Demonstration Project submitted by Beihang University are not contradictory to the Appraisal Certificate and are consistent with the contract in question. It should be held that Beihang University did not misrepresent the project products. The assertion by Qinzhou Ruifeng Company that Beihang University fabricated project products lacks basis and is not supported by this court.

(2) Regarding whether Beihang University misrepresented the technology development costs

The section "Fixed Asset Investment Estimate" on page 3 of the Application Report for the Demonstration Project records: "1. Raw material pretreatment system: RMB 30,000,000; 2. 40m diameter rotary hearth furnace reduction workshop: RMB 210,000,000; 3. Molten deep reduction and smelting slag for vanadium-iron separation system: RMB 65,000,000; ... 7. Project design, supervision, and other preliminary expenses: RMB 30,000,000 ..." Qinzhou Ruifeng Company argues that the sum of the above costs, minus the plant construction costs, equals the manufacturing cost of the entire industrial production line, being RMB 315,000,000. It claims that it entered into the contract in question with Beihang University for a total of RMB 315,000,000 based on this. However, the total cost for Beihang University to subcontract the production line manufacturing project to Xinye Company was only RMB 170,200,000. Therefore, it should be held that Beihang University falsely reported RMB 144,800,000 in project development costs. The court finds as follows: First, technology development costs include, but are not limited to, expenses related to test equipment. Although test equipment plays a critical role in technology development activities, it is far from the entirety of such activities. Especially in industrial test projects, in addition to test equipment, the overall design of the project, optimization of production processes, and monitoring of production flows are also critical, and the corresponding consideration for these can be included in technology development costs. Second, technology development costs are only one of the factors that determine the price of a technology development contract. Advancedness of the technological achievement, the degree of its implementation, transformation, and application, the rights and obligations of the parties, the economic benefits of the technological achievement, and similar factors, together with technology development costs, are important considerations in pricing a technology development contract. Therefore, in this case, the RMB 170,200,000 that Beihang University paid to subcontract the production line manufacturing project to Xinye Company is only part of the technology development costs for the industrialization demonstration project for vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology. Furthermore, these technology development costs are only one of the factors considered in pricing the entire contract. Qinzhou Ruifeng Company equating the manufacturing cost of the project production line with the entire technology development cost, and then equating the technology development cost with the contract price in question, is inconsistent both with the objective composition of technology development costs and with the basic principles of pricing technology development contracts. Its claim that Beihang University falsely reported technology development costs lacks basis and is not supported by this court.

In summary, the court finds that Beihang University fully informed Qinzhou Ruifeng Company of the true plan for the large-scale industrial test phase of the vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore comprehensive utilization technology. It did not commit fraud in relation to the research and development plan for the technology in question at this phase.

Given that Beihang University fully informed Qinzhou Ruifeng Company of the true situation of the semi-industrial test phase of the vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore comprehensive utilization technology, as well as the true plan for the industrialization demonstration project for vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology, the court finds that Beihang University did not commit fraud against Qinzhou Ruifeng Company.

(B) Regarding whether Qinzhou Ruifeng Company, induced by fraud, fell into error and, on that basis, made a declaration of intent contrary to its true will

As discussed above, technology research and development activities are phased and their outcomes are uncertain. In determining whether the commissioning party in a technology commission development contract, having been induced by fraud, fell into error and made a declaration of intent contrary to its true will, the inherent characteristics of technology development activities must be fully respected. Consideration should be given comprehensively to factors such as the commissioning party's cognitive ability regarding the contract project, its sources of information, and what it could reasonably have foreseen, in order to determine whether it fell into error, and whether there is a causal relationship between its error and the fraudulent conduct of the commissioned party.

In this case, as analyzed above, Beihang University did not commit fraud against Qinzhou Ruifeng Company. Therefore, there is no issue of Qinzhou Ruifeng Company having been induced by fraud to fall into error and make a declaration of intent contrary to its true will. Moreover, Qinzhou Ruifeng Company should have been clearly aware of the differences between the processes and products of the first phase of the industrialization demonstration project for vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology under the contract in question, and the vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore comprehensive utilization technology at the semi-industrial test phase recorded in the Appraisal Certificate. On this basis, it should have estimated the project output value, calculated the project costs, and made the commercial judgment of whether to enter into the contract in question.

1. Qinzhou Ruifeng Company should have been clearly aware of the differences between the processes and products of the first phase of the industrialization demonstration project for vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology under the contract in question, and the vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore comprehensive utilization technology at the semi-industrial test phase recorded in the Appraisal Certificate.

According to the facts now ascertained, before the signing of the contract in question, Hong Kong Ruifeng Company, the parent company of Qinzhou Ruifeng Company, had visited Beihang University multiple times to inspect the technology in question and had received from Beihang University the Application Report for the Demonstration Project and the Energy Efficiency Chapter for the Industrialization Demonstration Project for Vanadium-Titanium-Iron Separation Technology. In the Application Report for the Demonstration Project, concepts of "high-titanium slag" and "titanium slag" appeared simultaneously, and it stated that the product obtained after slag-iron separation in the industrial demonstration project was titanium slag, with a titanium dioxide content of 46%. As Qinzhou Ruifeng Company itself argued, according to the high-titanium slag industry standard promulgated by the National Development and Reform Commission, the titanium dioxide content in the lowest grade of high-titanium slag must be above 80%. Therefore, considering comprehensively the huge investment by Qinzhou Ruifeng Company in the project in question, its due diligence on the technology and project in question, its level of knowledge of relevant industry common sense, and the specific statements in the Application Report for the Demonstration Project, the court finds that before the signing of the contract in question, Qinzhou Ruifeng Company had already paid sufficient attention to the specific plan for the industrialization demonstration project for vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology and its differences from the vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore comprehensive utilization technology at the semi-industrial test phase recorded in the Appraisal Certificate. It possessed the ability to recognize these differences. Therefore, it should have been clearly aware that the products obtained from the first phase of the industrialization demonstration project for vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology under the contract in question were titanium slag, not high-titanium slag. This conclusion is also confirmed by the agreement in the Technology Development (Commission) Contract that the product after slag-iron separation is titanium slag, and that "the products of this contract are reduced iron, titanium slag (used for producing titanium dioxide, 98% or more), and vanadium slag (used for producing vanadium pentoxide, 98% or more)"; and by the agreement in the Technical Attachment that "Products: pig iron, titanium slag, vanadium slag (production of titanium dioxide and vanadium pentoxide will be determined by another contract)", "The reduced pellets are hot-charged into the smelting furnace for separation, yielding reduced molten iron, vanadium slag, and titanium slag", and "The products of this contract are reduced iron, titanium slag, and vanadium slag ... Titanium slag and vanadium slag are raw materials for future deep processing of vanadium and titanium, and their product specifications will be handled by another contract." Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's claim that it fell into error due to Beihang University's fraud, on the grounds that it did not know the difference between "high-titanium slag" and "titanium slag," clearly lacks basis and is not supported by this court.

2. Qinzhou Ruifeng Company should have itself estimated the project output value, calculated the project costs, and made the commercial judgment of whether to enter into the contract in question.

The large-scale industrial test phase is a critical phase for transforming science and technology into productive forces. In this phase, technology and capital are both indispensable. The investor and the technology provider should cooperate wholeheartedly based on each fulfilling their respective responsibilities, to withstand risks, solve problems, and achieve success. The judgment on whether to invest in a large-scale industrial test project, although inseparable from an understanding of the technology and the project, is essentially a commercial judgment. During the negotiation phase, the technology provider should ensure that the technology it supplies is not false and that the plans it makes contain no misrepresentations. As for estimating the project output value, calculating the project costs, and forecasting project profits and similar commercial analyses, these should naturally be completed by the investor itself. In this case, while Beihang University did provide a reference opinion on the commercial value of the industrialization demonstration project for vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology, the decision on whether to invest in that project should still have been Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's own commercial judgment. Given that, as discussed above, Beihang University truthfully and completely informed Qinzhou Ruifeng Company of the situation of the semi-industrial test phase of the vanadium-titanium magnetite sand ore comprehensive utilization technology and the plan for the industrialization demonstration project for vanadium-titanium-iron separation technology; and given that the products of the first phase of the project, such as reduced iron, titanium slag, and vanadium slag, as specified in the contract in question, are common products in the industry, the court finds that Qinzhou Ruifeng Company was fully capable of estimating the project output value on its own and, on that basis, judging whether entering into the contract in question for a price of RMB 315,000,000 was in its commercial interest. Qinzhou Ruifeng Company's claim that Beihang University falsely reported project costs and output value, causing it to fall into error, lacks basis and is not supported by this court.

In summary, the court finds that the contract in question does not constitute a contract concluded by one party by means of fraud, causing the other party to make a declaration of intent contrary to its true will. The appeal by Qinzhou Ruifeng Company requesting the rescission of the contract in question between it and Beihang University cannot be sustained and should be dismissed. The judgment of the first instance has clear findings of fact and correct application of law, and should be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

Appeal dismissed, and the original judgment affirmed.

The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 1,466,800 shall be borne by Qinzhou Ruifeng Vanadium-Titanium-Iron Technology Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
